---
applyTo: "app/*/migrations/**/*.py,app/sep/apps/*/migrations/**/*.py"
---

# Database Migrations

SEP has three independent Alembic migration tracks, one per sub-application. Each track has its own `alembic_version_*` table and own `env.py`.

| Service | Script directory | Version table |
|---|---|---|
| SEP | `app/sep/migrations/` | `alembic_version_sep` |
| Inventory | `app/inventory/migrations/` | `alembic_version_inventory` |
| Tasks | `app/tasks/migrations/` | `alembic_version_tasks` |

## What to check

CI runs `make checkmigrations` on every PR — it catches missing migrations and out-of-date heads automatically. Don't manually flag "model changed but no migration": CI already does. Focus on the manual-judgment items below.

- **Migration lives in the right track.** A model change under `app/sep/` MUST have its migration in `app/sep/migrations/versions/` (or under `app/sep/apps/<name>/migrations/versions/` for a sub-app that owns its own chain — those dirs are auto-listed in `[sep] version_locations` by `scripts/sync_alembic_version_locations.py`), NOT under `app/tasks/migrations/` or `app/inventory/migrations/`. Cross-track placement is a hard fail — the migration won't run on the right database.
- **Deleting a sub-app's migration chain is an explicit step.** The sync script refuses to drop an entry already listed in `[sep] version_locations`, because that configured-but-absent path is how the orphan-head filter recognises a stripped app. A deliberate deletion needs `python scripts/sync_alembic_version_locations.py --allow-removals`; anything else (a locally stripped app, a half-deleted package) should restore the directory instead.
- **`upgrade()` and `downgrade()` are both implemented.** Empty `downgrade()` (just `pass`) is a red flag — migrations must be reversible.
- **`downgrade()` reverses `upgrade()`.** New tables in `upgrade()` need `op.drop_table()` in `downgrade()`; new columns need `op.drop_column()`; new indexes need `op.drop_index()`. The pair must be symmetric. A `downgrade()` that re-narrows a column's allowed domain (removes enum members, re-adds `NOT NULL`, shrinks `VARCHAR` length) must first `DELETE`/`UPDATE` rows holding the now-invalid values — otherwise it aborts at runtime the moment such data exists.
- **No data loss without a written strategy.** `op.drop_table()` or `op.drop_column()` on a column that has live data needs an explicit data-migration step (or a justification in the PR description). Same for column type changes that may truncate (`TEXT` → `INTEGER`, `VARCHAR(255)` → `VARCHAR(50)`). A parser branch or deserializer that silently remaps an old stored value at read time is NOT a substitute for a one-shot data migration (`UPDATE`/`DELETE`) — flag it.
- **Column additions on existing tables** must be nullable OR have a server-side default. Non-nullable adds on a populated table will fail at upgrade time. Flag any `op.add_column(..., sa.Column(..., nullable=False))` without a `server_default`. Also flag a new table whose every non-key column is nullable — if a row with nothing populated is meaningless, the migration needs `nullable=False` on at least one required column or a `CheckConstraint`.
- **Index changes are intentional.** Flag unjustified `op.create_index` or `op.drop_index` — they affect production performance. Confirm the index serves a query the diff introduces or removes. Also flag a single-column `op.create_index` / `index=True` on a column already the leading column of a composite index or unique constraint — the composite left-prefix-covers it, so the standalone index only adds write cost.
- **Foreign key constraints** declare `ondelete=` explicitly (`CASCADE`, `SET NULL`, `RESTRICT`). Don't accept FK additions that fall through to the default.
- **Renames are dangerous.** Renaming columns or tables breaks running code during rolling deployment. Flag any `op.alter_column(... new_column_name=...)` or `op.rename_table(...)`. Acceptable only when explicitly coordinated (the PR description names the deployment plan).

## File naming

Generated by Alembic from the configured template; format is `%%(year)d_%%(month).2d_%%(day).2d_%%(hour).2d%%(minute).2d-%%(rev)s_%%(slug)s` (Alembic appends `.py`; the resolved filename ends `…%%(slug)s.py`). Flag manually-written filenames that don't match (timestamp prefix is load-bearing — it orders the migration history).

## env.py expectations

Each track's `env.py` imports its own models and settings, uses `async_engine_from_config`, and points `target_metadata` at `SQLModel.metadata`. Don't accept diffs that point one track's `env.py` at another track's models or metadata. Each `env.py` also imports `compare_type` from `app/core/db/utils` and passes it to the `run_migrations_*` calls — don't accept a diff that drops or replaces it. A cross-package model imported **solely** to register with `SQLModel.metadata` belongs in `env.py`, not in a service `models.py` with `# noqa: F401`; flag such a registration-only import in a `models.py`.
